findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator cannot paginate datetime ordering
findings.body: In src/sentry/api/paginator.py line 840, OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key does int(math.floor(value))/int(math.ceil(value)) on the sort-key attribute. The only caller added in this PR (src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py line 80) uses order_by="-datetime", so value is a datetime.datetime, not a number, which raises TypeError on every page. Even if it did not raise, value_from_cursor returns the raw integer cursor value while build_queryset compares it against a datetime column with >=/<=, producing type-mismatched SQL or wrong pages. Consequence: the new optimized path always 500s or returns incorrect audit-log pages.

findings.title: Negative queryset slicing is unsupported and attacker-triggerable
findings.body: In src/sentry/api/paginator.py line 882, when enable_advanced_features is true and cursor.offset < 0 the code executes list(queryset[start_offset:stop]) with a negative start_offset. Django QuerySets explicitly do not support negative indexing/slicing and raise AssertionError, contrary to the inline comment claiming Django handles it automatically. Cursor strings of the form value:offset:is_prev are client-controlled via Cursor.from_string, so a caller of the new optimized_pagination=true path can craft a negative-offset cursor to trigger an unhandled 500 (DoS). If the slice ever operated on a list, negative start would wrap around and return tail rows outside the requested page, breaking completeness of audit logs.

findings.title: BasePaginator still passes negative offsets for prev cursors
findings.body: In src/sentry/api/paginator.py line 182, BasePaginator.get_result now does start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset, so forward pagination clamps negatives but prev-page (is_prev=True) pagination passes the raw negative offset to queryset[start_offset:stop]. This still hits Django's unsupported negative-slice path and raises AssertionError on a crafted prev cursor, turning all existing cursor-paginated endpoints into a 500 instead of rejecting the cursor. The later check len(results) == offset + limit + extra also uses the negative offset, so prev-page extra-row trimming is mathematically wrong even if slicing succeeded, causing duplicated or missing rows.

findings.title: Untested privileged pagination path for compliance-critical logs
findings.body: In src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py lines 70-83, a new public query parameter optimized_pagination=true switches audit-log listing from DateTimePaginator to OptimizedCursorPaginator for superusers or members with global access. No tests are added for the branch or for OptimizedCursorPaginator, despite audit logs being compliance-critical. Consequence: a broken datetime-incompatible paginator with unsafe offset handling is exposed to privileged viewers without coverage, risking outages and incomplete/duplicated audit history going undetected.
